8/3/2025 Lunging at kennel door when approached. Cannot be handled. Partial on catchpole. (alarm barking, growling and hard staring)

8/10/2025 Approached Stav (Rama) from inside portion of his run. He presented with barrier reactivity. I let him go out to the outside portion of the run. I knelt down to his level and offered treats. He was not interested in my treats and instead he got so nervous he urinated. I sat on the ground with my back facing away from him and allowed him to get familiar with my presence. He would occasionally come up to the gate to see what I was doing but then immediately retracted to the back of the kennel. He would low growl with whale eyes if I turned around. Realizing that he was more scared then anything, I cracked the run door open to see if he would approach. As soon as the run door opened and I offered my hand for a sniff, he approached me with a low-wagging tail. I offered him my leash to which he lowered his head and allowed me to put it on. Exited the kennel and walked to the mulch yard. When we got into the mulch yard, I let him roam around (with the leash still on). I sat on the bench and allowed him to approach me if he wanted. I observed that he was heavily panting due to stress. However, he would approach me with a wagging tail and allow me to pet his head and back. We left the mulch yard and went for a walk to the next yard over where he did a fence greeting with Bubba Boy. He seemed excited to meet another dog and I suspect he is dog friendly. We then walked inside and I brought him over to the supervisor desk. He stopped midway to greet two customers in which he offered submissive ears and a tail wag. Once at the desk, he was met by a few kennel techs. While he did show some shyness, he allowed one kennel tech to pet his head. We went back to 200, I placed him back in his kennel and unleashed without incident. Recommend L3-SF and a playgroup assessment.

As soon as the run door opened and I offered my hand for a sniff, he approached me with a low-wagging tail. I offered him my leash to which he lowered his head and allowed me to put it on. Exited the kennel and walked to the mulch yard. When we got into the mulch yard, I let him roam around (with the leash still on). I sat on the bench and allowed him to approach me if he wanted. I observed that he was heavily panting due to stress. However, he would approach me with a wagging tail and allow me to pet his head and back. We left the mulch yard and went for a walk to the next yard over where he did a fence greeting with Bubba Boy. He seemed excited to meet another dog and I suspect he is dog friendly. We then walked inside and I brought him over to the supervisor desk. He stopped midway to greet two customers in which he offered submissive ears and a tail wag. Once at the desk, he was met by a few kennel techs. While he did show some shyness, he allowed one kennel tech to pet his head. We went back to 200, I placed him back in his kennel and unleashed without incident. Recommend L3-SF and a playgroup assessment.

Behavior Notes_y:
7/31/2025 easily handled in the kennel. Once in the exam room was very nervous and would startle easily. Hard stares and whips head at you when startled. Wasn't able to get muzzle on so only did partial exam with catch pole. Startles easilyHard staringhead whipping

8/7/2025 On 8/2 I did an adoption meet and greet with Rotsalot. The first time I went to get him from intake, he was laying down when I approached the gate (it was VERY loud in the room, with the other dogs barking). He remained when I approached. I spoke softly to him, and opened the gate. I offered my leash, and he hesitated/stiffened slightly, but let me put the leash on. Once on leash, he was easily handled. He walked through the crowded intake room no problem, despite crates being everywhere. I met the adopter in the yard, and Rotsalot walked up to him after sniffing around. I will note that the adopter has pet sit Rots a few times, but the adopter pet him all over (face, legs, torso) with no problem. After, I returned him to the kennel with no issues unleashing.At the second meet and greet, Rots was again easy to handle. The same adopter was present, along with a woman. Rotsalot allowed the woman to pet him as well, and Rots approached me for pets as well. Today, 8/5, while passing out meds in intake, I approached Rots kennel, and offered my hands for a sniff. He licked them, and leaned his body against the bars to ask for pets. I pet him through the gate bars.I know he had issues with vetting, so I'm recommending a change from L3 - BH to L2 - BH. Taken out on 8.8.2025 and did well on the leash.  He stopped to sniff other dogs through the gates and gave them no other reaction.  Taken to the yard he did well with full body pets, even on the feet.  Because of previous issues it is best to have caution with a breed this large and so we will move him to L2-BH and recommend still using caution for any sort of vet restraint or nail trims etc. -CW

6/2/2024 Very BR but when he comes out is sweet. Was doing intake and went to scan him with the microchip scanner and he started showing his teeth and his hackles went up. Micky came in and catch poled him and put him back in the kennel.

6/3/2024 Growling hard staring showing teeth barrier reactive

6/8/2024 very food motivated. Started with low growling and baring teeth at the door. I offered a few treats and he loosened up completely. Allowed for brief pets on the head and ears. Would low growl again when door opened. Did not attempt to retrieve today but appears willing to interact with people. Re-check later. 

6/11/2024 Still growling at gate. 

9/17/2024 gave treats through kennel, displayed loose body, relaxed ears/mouth. treat motivated. all dogs were in exterior portion of their kennel, sterling was brought into interior portion and he allowed us to leash and remove him from his kennel. pulls hard on leash, attempts to choose path. when given verbal correction he stopped pulling on leash momentarily. brought him to pasture where he remained on leash. explored pasture, showed high interest in chicken coop, no interest in mower that was far out in pasture. allowed shannon to give treats, sat for treats, and allowed full body pets and head pets. showed minor interest in playing with toys. loose body language throughout duration of interaction. eager to get back inside. when placed in kennel allowed me to enter kennel with him and remove leash without issue. -gillian flebbe

9/23/2024 displayed long stroked wagging tail, eagerly took treat when offered. -gillian flebbe

10/26/2024 greeted him in yard. met me at gate, ears laid softly against head, relaxed pant, allowed me to pet his entire body and give him butt slaps. ran back and forth between me and the gate, was able to recall to me when fixating on another dog. got zoomies and was able to entice to play. he began mouthing on my sleeve and attempting to play tug of war with it, i corrected him, offered leash tugs and physically removed my sleeve from him but he continued to grab my sleeve until i removed myself from run. bite inhibition good but does not listen to verbal corrections. 

10/29/2024 sterling, rock lee, and remson got loose from their exterior kennels this morning. sterling locked onto remson's neck and pinned him down. remson was unable to escape and sterling would not refocus. madison, shelby, and todd came by to break up the dogs. (rock lee observed incident and ran into an open kennel where todd was able to secure him) catch pole placed around remson and madison grabbed hold of sterlings rear legs, eventually getting him to detach from remson. at that point sterling was catch poled and replaced in his kennel. he began biting the catch pole and would not release. todd sprayed sterling with the hose to coerce him to drop catch pole but sterling did not appear phased nor would he redirect. he was frantically biting catch pole, bleeding profusely at the mouth, and panting heavily with a wide mouth. eventually released catch pole but was panting heavily with wide mouth and elongated tongue, pacing and looking everywhere but at todd and i who were standing directly in front of kennel at his eye level. coerced him into interior portion of run where he displayed similar behavior and remained standing at front of his kennel looking everywhere. placing a "do not remove from kennel" sign on his run as he has many incidences where he has escaped his run and been extremely difficult to replace into kennel, he is aggressive with other dogs, and although appears to have good bite inhibition, his mouthiness is still very strong and he is a very strong dog. considering recent interactions, it appears sterling is displaying frustration behaviors and no methods of soothing works for him, he stays amped up for extended periods of time and is unresponsive to verbal direction.  unknown how dogs kennels were opened as they were secured when i walked by and interacted with 200 dogs 30 minutes prior, all kennel doors of escaped dogs were opened outward.

He enjoyed getting his ears cleaned and getting ointment put on his scabs, leaning into Dr. C massaging the ointment into his skin. No concerns while giving shots. Walked back to kennel, still unreactive to other dogs, approached some dogs through the glass in flex, body remaining relaxed, tail low wagging. 8/9/2025 while in intake bores teeth, growls, alarm barks, and air snaps when kennel door is approached. partial on catchpole

8/18/2025 Approached Loki from the inside portion of his kennel and offered treats. He came up from the back of the kennel and took the treats from my hand. I then let him outside as his neighbors were being loud. Once outside I approached him and he came to the gate when treats were present. I allowed him to sniff my hand through the gate. He licked it a few times and allowed me to pet his snout and top of head through the kennel bars. He comes across very stiff and stand-offish and can sometimes give a side eye. I opened his kennel door and offered him my leash. He saw the leash and retreated to the back of the kennel. I then threw a treat in his kennel to get him to move closer. When he got closer to me, I offered him a treat from the palm of my hand, which he took easily. I offered him my leash again, this time with a treat and he stepped close enough to allow me to slip the leash on. He exited the kennel and immediately went to pee (poss super holder?). We walked to the patchy grass area where he went to the bathroom again. I then walked him over to the 200 mulch yards and allowed him to roam around. I first let him get familiar with the area on leash. Once I felt comfortable, I dropped the leash and allowed him to roam. While sitting on the bench he explored the yard. I called him over to me in which he came and stuck his head between my legs to solicit a pet. I then was able to remove his leash and collar that he still had on. I then took the leash off of him and allowed him to roam freely. He used the bathroom a bunch more times (needs neuter!). He then went to the yard gate and stood by waiting for me to leash him back up. I leashed him with no issues and then walked him inside. Once inside we walked down the 200 hall and out towards the supervisor desk. I took him to clinic to scan for a chip just in case one was missed (no chip). He stiffened up when I scanned him but showed no aggression. I then walked him past Ashley and Jade at the supervisor desk where he willingly walked up to both of them for a sniff. Ashley offered him a treat, which he turned down but he allowed Jade to pet his head. We then walked back to his kennel and I placed him back in. I took his leash off with no issues. When I was walking away to go let him back inside, he started crying (i've only every heard him growl). I let him inside through the guillotine. When he came in he still had loose, wiggly body language. Rec L3-SF and move out of 200

8/18/2025 L3-SF, see focus group notes

8/19/2025 L3-SF, see focus group notes Leveled down to L3-SF based on Focus group notes - NAOMI

7/29/2025 Lorain was stiff, whale eyed and alarm barking when we initially approached her. There were dogs across from her that were barking and making her anxious so we moved those dogs out of view and placed a crate bottom to block the dog next to her. She hesitantly accepted treats at first but then started to retreat while growling again. I opened the kennel door completely to help her feel less corner and she would approach the door, then retreat. She repeated this twice. I decided to use a catchpole to at least attempt to get her out of the kennel. She bowed her head and was avoidant when she saw the pole but I opened the loop as wide as I could and let her place her head in it when she turned. Once on the catchpole she walked on it without lashing out but was very stiff. Once out in the garage area she sniffed around and seemed to loosen a bit so I fed the leash over the catchpole then removed the pole once the leash was secure. I let her walk around for a few seconds before squatting down on the ground and she ran into my lap and solicited attention eagerly. She let me pet her all over. I was able to get her harness off and she seemed to loosen up even further once that was taken off. She then solicited attention from Maddie and was generally very friendly with the staff in intake once we walked her by the desk and was friendly with people passing her in the hall, albeit a bit unsure (she would pause at first then loosen up after scooting a little closer to me.). She readily solicited attention from me a few more times and jumped into my lap a couple of times in the hallway while we waited for a spot in 301 to open. Moved her into 301 and requested a level down from Emma. Moved from STAFF ONLY to L3 SF today. 

7/29/2025 Emma approved after successful FG.

I had my niece sleep over and Scarlet was immediately friendly and fine with her for several hours. She did push my dog to the ground when he came near her bowl (he was fine, no bites or anything). He's blind and deaf and missed her warning growl when she was telling him to back off of her food. We had fed them in separate areas with supervision, but my husband didn't understand the growling Scarlet was doing was a warning. She has shown zero food aggression with me personally handling her food.Has this dog ever injured another dog? If yes, please describe the incident. 8/21/2025 8/21/25Hi there,Here are notes about Whiskey during this week-long evaluation.  We can keep him for a few more days, possibly returning him on Sunday or Monday - still working on the logistics as we will be traveling next week and I know Tuesdays are rough and I want to continue to set him up for success as much as possible.Home set-up:Whiskey was housed in a separate room, away from our 2 resident dogs.  The room is double gated at the door - a baby gate at the threshold and a removable gate to add more distance from my resident dog's noisy eyes to the entrance of the room.  The room is on the third floor of our townhome and was set-up with cameras for additional monitoring.  The loudest the room would get would be when I was home and on work calls.  We also had an air filter running all day, on it's highest setting it can be loud, but seemed like white noise.When Whiskey needed to go out/downstairs for a walk or to go potty, our 2 residents dogs were crated and secured in a space on the main floor where Whiskey could not approach their gates directly.  The ground floor is my husband's space and where he works.  We practiced crate and rotate in our home while Whiskey was with us.Daily routine:Whiskey was taken out 3-4 times a day, depending if I went to the office.  Frequent breaks ensured he did not go potty in the house.  When at home, one of those outings would be a lunch-time or early afternoon 10-15 minute walk outside.  Whiskey was fed 2x a day, breakfast and dinner.  When working from home, I would crate him after breakfast and after his lunch-time walk, I would have him roam the room free while I continued to work. After dinner, I let Whiskey have the room on his own, uncrated.  He usually just lay on the floor and watched the door until I came back.  He would be crated overnight as he slept.Health notes:Whiskey still coughs, but there are no signs of phlegm and his nose is no longer runny/mucus-y.  His coughs happen mostly when he has just woken up or when he's walking up and down the stairs.  He is still taking doxy in the AM along with his breakfast.  He is still butt scoots on occasion.  His nose and paws are very dry though, they feel scratchy. Pus still continues to show up around his eyes, though not as much as when he first got here - but still present.  He seems to have some stiffness in his rear legs though.Eyesight:I think Whiskey can see shadows, the bigger the item the better he can maneuver around it or at least know that it's there.  He still walks down steps tentatively, but I've noticed that he prefers to walk along the stair wall, I'm assuming it helps him navigate.  He also seems to navigate better in bright light vs. a dark room.I don't know if it's eyesight or spatial distancing might be his issue or both, but sometimes he will run right into me in the backyard because he didn't realize I was right there.  He often missteps when coming to a curb. He may also flinch when you pet him on the head or under his chin because he didn't see your hand coming.General behavior:Talking - When he does make a sound, he roos or makes deep vocal grunts.  It can sound growly, but as you get to know him, it's not a growl or at least not a warning one.  He's usually vocal when we are outside or when I'm with him upstairs and playing with him and his toys.On-leash - He can pull, but he's getting better at not pulling too hard.  When he pulls, it's because something got his attention, curiosity, or interest.  Dogs walking (or barking), people walking by, strollers nearby, cats, etc.Leash-biting - Only showed leash biting when we swapped leash to a slip lead vs. leash with a clasp to his collar.  He initially attempted leash biting when you try to put the slip lead over his head. If you dangle the other end of the leash in front of him, he has tried to grab it.  To curb this, we've sprayed the slip lead with bitter apple spray and also use special treats to reward him when we can put on/take off the leash with minimal to none LB behavior.  We have also rewarded him when he lets go of the leash, if he was able to get a hold of it.  I have noticed that when the slip lead is loop is big enough where it can go over his head without him touching it on the sides of his face, it is easier and quicker to get the leash on.Potty-trained:  Whiskey is potty-trained, though it may take a few days for him to learn where he can go.  We aim to have him go out 4x a day to prevent any accidents, though 3x a day can also work where he was taken out in the morning, when I got home from work, and before going to bed.Crate-trained:  Whiskey does well in a crate and has learned to go inside on his own by tapping on the top of the crate.  Since the time he's been with us, he's only barked once in the crate, and that was during a thunderstorm. He only barked once and then was able to settle.  As he got healthier/felt safer, he midly whines when he is in the crate but still sees you near. It's more of a muffled whine, but he does not do it long and then just lays down in the crate to sleep.Treats - Whiskey is a gentle treat taker, because of his sight issues, he may need a visual cue to listen to where the treat is.  The best treats for him are smelly ones.Interactions:Other people in the home/men:  He has responded well to my husband who has given Whiskey pets and treats. My husband would come up to the baby gate where Whiskey would come up and seek pets.  Whiskey would also go up to my husband on his own when my husband was at his desk to seek pets.Kids:  We have not had him directly near kids or interact with kids.  The closest to a kid he has been was walking by the community pool on a weekend.  These were mostly small/younger kids, but a few were screaming very loudly that it made Whiskey anxious.  He pulled me towards the pool gate and attempted to try to put his head through the fence. I'm not sure if he had the intention to go through the fence or if he just couldn't tell/see a fence existed.Cats: We bumped into a neighborhood cat who was more scared of  Whiskey than Whiskey was of the cat.  Whiskey showed some interest, but I was able to call him towards me before we continued our walk.Dogs:  Both resident dogs seem curious about Whiskey, but we did not allow any type of meet and greet or walks together.  Reese (our female dog) would watch him through the baby gate+secondary gate.  When he knows she's there he will go over to the doorway.  On the second day, it seemed like he was about to make an attempt to jump on the baby gate to get a better look at Reese, but I told him "no" and got him to go back into his crate.  He hasn't tried it since.Toys and things:  Whiskey seems to prefer crinkly type toys the best, though eh has been caught licking or mouthing at sheets/towels we used to catch any potty accidents.  He's not tearing or destroying anything, just lightly mouthing/nibbling.Suggestions:If Whiskey is unable to find placement out of the shelter, it's unclear if he will regress/decline once he's back at the shelter. Considering his stressors, this could be highlly likely.  If possible, he may do well in one of the flex rooms as they have more room and tend to be a lot quieter than the runs.

The DFTD was comfortable with taking a hard puller on leash and energetic dog for a trail walk (limited visual on other dogs) so we decided he needed to get out of the kennel for a bit. He did not mouth or bite at any point in the interactions, just very jumpy with high energy spins. Use treats to retrieve from kennel and monitor barrier reactivity. BR observed and level of OA in office is notably concerning. Currently leveled as a L2-OA/JM. Including BR in level.
